setup: Lie on your back, hands lightly by your head
Lift your knees over your hips
Curl your head and shoulders slightly up
execution: Turn one shoulder toward the opposite knee
Straighten the other leg out, low and long
Keep your lower back on the floor
faults: Don't yank your head with your hands
Don't just flap your elbows across
Don't race; slow reps work harder

notes: The turn comes from the ribs, not from pulling the elbow across with the arm.
Move at a steady pace; fast, jerky reps are hard to control and easy to do badly.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Crunch
regressions.reason: Learn the curl without the twist and leg work.

regressions.name: Dead bug
regressions.reason: Same alternating legs with the back still and no curl.

progressions.name: Bicycle crunch with a pause
progressions.reason: Hold each twist for a second or two.

substitutions.name: Cable woodchop
substitutions.reason: Loaded rotation standing at a cable column.

substitutions.name: Pallof press
substitutions.reason: Trains the obliques by resisting a twist.

substitutions.name: Side plank
substitutions.reason: Side-of-waist work with the spine still.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at floor level, figure lying along the frame with the head on the left. The near elbow reaching across toward the far knee shows the twist; keep the head end slightly raised so the shoulder lift reads.

keyPositions.label: Near knee in
keyPositions.describe: Head and shoulders curled up. Near knee drawn toward the chest; far leg extended long and low, off the mat. Torso turned so the far elbow reaches toward the near knee.

keyPositions.label: Switch
keyPositions.describe: Both knees passing at mid-range, torso turning through the middle, shoulders still curled up.

keyPositions.label: Far knee in
keyPositions.describe: Mirror of Near knee in: far knee toward the chest, near leg extended long, torso turned the other way.

ikHints: Lower back and pelvis stay on the mat in every frame
Hands rest lightly by the head; elbows stay wide
emphasise: Shoulder turns toward the opposite knee
The straight leg stays low and long
doNotShow: Lower back arching off the mat

sources.title: ACE Exercise Library: Supine Bicycle Crunches
ACE press release (2001): ACE-sponsored study reveals best and worst abdominal exercises
sources.supports: primaryMuscles (the bicycle ranked first for rectus abdominis and second for obliques by EMG, 30 adults)
sources.note: Press release, not a peer-reviewed paper. Muscle activity is not the same as growth.

uncertain.note: JEFIT and ExRx call this "Air bike", which is the catalogue name of the fan bike (expansion research Q6). It is deliberately not an alias here; an imported "Air Bike" filed under abs should be confirmed by Ben.
Reps are usually counted as total touches (both sides). Some people count one per pair; the entry doesn't fix which.
StrengthLog lists the hip flexors as secondary; they are listed as secondary here (vocabulary word added 23 Oct 2026, expansion research Q1).
Uses a stride tempo for the alternating legs. trunkRotation signs are drawing conventions only, and the angles are approximate drawing targets, not measured data.
